tokens.title: Double‑check query spelling/case on empty search results
tokens.content: If repo_search returns zero matches, verify that the search term matches the identifier’s spelling and case; a typo or case mismatch can look a false missing‑coverage signal.

tokens.title: Extract minimal context with repo_read after locating an export
tokens.content: After repo_search shows the line number of an uncovered function, call repo_read with a small start‑end range (e.g., the line itself and a couple around it) to include a concise snippet in the report.

tokens.title: Target file path in repo_search for quick export lookup
tokens.content: Give repo_search the exact file (e.g., src/audit.ts) when you need to list its exported functions; this avoids scanning the whole repo and returns precise matches instantly.

tokens.title: Read test imports before searching for coverage
tokens.content: Open the test files with repo_read to list the functions they import, then compare that list to the exported symbols gathered from src files. Any exported function not appearing in the imports list is likely untested.

tokens.title: Scope repo_search to target directories
tokens.content: Run repo_search with an empty path to locate the source file, then repeat the search within the test folder only. Narrowing the path for the second search speeds up the query and prevents false positives from unrelated directories.

tokens.title: Fetch only relevant source lines
tokens.content: When confirming an export, call repo_read with a narrow start‑end window around the declaration instead of the whole file. This reduces output size, speeds up the run, and avoids unrelated code clutter.

tokens.title: Use exact‑match queries to avoid substring false positives
tokens.content: When searching for a function name, surround the query with word boundaries or quotes (e.g., "recoverFrom") to ensure the search matches the identifier itself and not longer names that contain it. This yields cleaner evidence and reduces manual filtering.

tokens.title: Validate import statements in test files before searching for usage
tokens.content: Read the first few lines of the relevant test file (repo_read) to see how the function is imported. Knowing the exact import path prevents false‑negative searches caused by mismatched identifiers or aliasing.

tokens.title: Broaden symbol search to the whole repository when test‑folder search is empty
tokens.content: If a repo_search in the tests folder finds no matches for an exported name, run another repo_search with an empty path (searching the entire repo) to confirm the symbol truly has no references elsewhere. This avoids missing indirect imports or usage outside the test directory.

tokens.title: Report exact line location of uncovered export
tokens.content: After finding an exported function with no test matches, use repo_read to capture its line number and include that line in the output. This lets developers jump straight to the definition and add tests efficiently.

tokens.title: Read source around the export to confirm exact name before searching
tokens.content: Use repo_read to display a few lines of the source file around the export declaration. Knowing the precise identifier prevents false‑negative searches in tests.

tokens.title: Treat empty search results as evidence of missing references
tokens.content: If repo_search reports zero matches for a symbol in the test directory, interpret it as a lack of test coverage rather than a tool error. This avoids overlooking untested code.

tokens.title: Search exported symbols then verify test usage
tokens.content: Run a repo_search for the source file to list exported names, then run another repo_search in the test folder for each name. If the second search returns no matches, the export lacks tests. This two‑step search is fast and reliable for coverage checks.
